title: Ecclesiastes Bible Quiz - Chapter 1
description: Ten questions on Ecclesiastes 1: the Preacher's words, vanity of vanities, the circuits of sun, wind and rivers, and the grief of much wisdom.

questions.text: How is the Preacher described in the first verse?
questions.explanation: The book opens with the words of the Preacher, the son of David, king in Jerusalem.

answers.text: The son of Jakeh, king in Israel
A shepherd from the hills of Jerusalem
The son of David, king in Jerusalem
A prophet sent to the king in Jerusalem

questions.text: What does the Preacher say in the second verse?
questions.explanation: The Preacher says: 'Vanity of vanities, vanity of vanities, all is vanity.'

answers.text: "The fear of Yahweh is the beginning of knowledge"

questions.text: One generation goes and another comes, but what remains forever?
questions.explanation: The verse says one generation goes and another generation comes, but the earth remains forever.

questions.text: What does the sun do after it goes down, according to this chapter?
questions.explanation: The verse says the sun rises and goes down, and hurries to its place where it rises.

answers.text: It rests in the depths of the sea
It hurries to its place where it rises
It turns around toward the north
It is never seen in its place again

questions.text: All the rivers run into the sea, yet what does this chapter say about the sea?
questions.explanation: The verse says all the rivers run into the sea, yet the sea is not full.

answers.text: The sea turns the rivers back

questions.text: What does this chapter say the eye is not satisfied with?
questions.explanation: The verse says the eye is not satisfied with seeing, nor the ear filled with hearing.

questions.text: What does this chapter say there is none of under the sun?
questions.explanation: The verse says that which has been is that which shall be, and there is no new thing under the sun.

questions.text: Having seen all the works done under the sun, what does the Preacher call them?
questions.explanation: He says: behold, all is vanity and a chasing after wind.

answers.text: A heavy yoke on the nations
Vanity and a chasing after wind
The gift of God to men

questions.text: Besides wisdom, what did the Preacher apply his heart to know?
questions.explanation: He says he applied his heart to know wisdom, and to know madness and folly, and perceived that this also was a chasing after wind.

questions.text: What does he who increases knowledge increase, according to the last verse?
questions.explanation: The verse says that in much wisdom is much grief, and he who increases knowledge increases sorrow.
